{{ElectionsRI}}
The '''2026 Rhode Island gubernatorial election''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect the [[governor of Rhode Island]]. Incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] governor [[Dan McKee]] ran for re-election to a second full term but was defeated in the primary by [[Helena Buonanno Foulkes|Helena Foulkes]]. [[Primary elections]] took place on September 9, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|date=September 26, 2025|title=2026 State Primary Election Dates|url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2026-state-primary-election-dates|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260509222424/https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2026-state-primary-election-dates|archive-date=May 9, 2026|url-status=live|access-date=September 27, 2025|website=[[National Conference of State Legislatures]]}}</ref> 

Republicans have not won a statewide election in Rhode Island since [[2006 Rhode Island gubernatorial election|2006]]. While Rhode Island is generally a safely Democratic state, the Democratic primary was predicted to be competitive due to McKee's high unpopularity<ref name="politico-20260808" />. The election has also been noted as not following national trends of progressives versus moderates, with both Democrats being relatively moderate and the primary instead largely boiling down to anger over the longtime closure of the [[Washington Bridge (Providence, Rhode Island)|Washington Bridge]].<ref name="politico-20260808">{{Cite web |last1=Okun |first1=Eli |date=August 8, 2026 |title=Why Rhode Island may oust a sitting governor over a bridge |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/08/08/rhode-island-governor-bridge-01030024 |access-date=2026-08-12 |website=POLITICO |language=en}}</ref>

This is the first election since [[2014 Hawaii gubernatorial election|2014]] in which an elected state governor lost renomination.{{efn|Governor [[Jeff Colyer]] of Kansas, who had taken office after the resignation of [[Sam Brownback]], was defeated by [[Kris Kobach]] in the [[2018 Kansas gubernatorial election|2018]] Republican primary election.}} It is also the first time since [[1994 Rhode Island gubernatorial election|1994]] in which an incumbent governor of Rhode Island lost renomination.

==Republican primary==
2022 lieutenant governor nominee Aaron Guckian defeated actress Elaine Pelino for the Republican nomination. Pelino requested a recount, which was approved by the Rhode Island Board of Elections, however it did not change the outcome.<ref>{{Cite web |last=NEWS |first=NBC 10 |date=2026-09-15 |title=Recount does not change outcome of Republican primary in governor's race |url=https://turnto10.com/news/local/officials-begin-recount-of-republican-primary-for-rhode-island-governor-sept-15-2026 |access-date=2026-09-15 |website=WJAR |language=en}}</ref>

===Candidates===
====Nominee====
*Aaron Guckian, former chair of the [[Warwick, Rhode Island|Warwick]] Sewer Authority and nominee for lieutenant governor in [[2022 Rhode Island lieutenant gubernatorial election|2022]]<ref name="Pelino"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Republican Guckian Is Running for Governor |url=https://www.golocalprov.com/politics/Republican-Guckian-Is-Running-for-Governor |access-date=November 30, 2025 |work=[[GoLocalProv]] |date=November 30, 2025}}</ref>

====Eliminated in primary====
*Elaine Pelino, former actress and model<ref name="Pelino">{{cite web |last=Baccari |first=Raymond |url=https://www.wpri.com/news/elections/republican-elaine-pelino-is-running-for-ri-governor-next-year/ |title=Republican Elaine Pelino is running for RI governor next year |date=November 14, 2025|access-date=February 26, 2026|publisher=[[WPRI-TV|WPRI]].com}}</ref>

====Disqualified====
*Robert Raimondo, businessman and cousin of former Democratic Governor [[Gina Raimondo]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Allen |first=Christopher |date=November 20, 2025 |title=Robert Raimondo enters R.I. governor's race |url=https://pbn.com/robert-raimondo-enters-r-i-governors-race/ |access-date=November 20, 2025 |website=Providence Business News |language=en-US}}</ref>

====Declined====
*[[Jessica de la Cruz]], minority leader of the [[Rhode Island Senate]] (2022–present) from the 23rd district (2019–present) ''([[2026 Rhode Island Senate election|running for re-election]])''<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kalunian |first=Kim |last2=Baccari |first2=Raymond |date=2026-01-21 |title=Community Focus: RI Senate Minority Leader Jessica de la Cruz |url=https://www.wpri.com/news/local-news/community-focus/community-focus-ri-senate-minority-leader-jessica-de-la-cruz-3/ |access-date=2026-01-21 |website=WPRI 12 News}}</ref>
*[[Kenneth Hopkins]], mayor of [[Cranston, Rhode Island|Cranston]] (2021–present)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wpri.com/news/local-news/ted-nesi/nesis-notes-july-19/|title=Nesi's Notes: July 19|last=Nesi|first=Ted|date=July 19, 2025|access-date=July 22, 2025|website=[[WPRI-TV]]}}</ref>
